# Environmental qualification plan

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Document | TP-001 of the compliance register |
| Standard | RTCA DO-160G / EUROCAE ED-14G |
| Revision | A |
| Installation | EO/IR installation kit on a CS-27 class platform |

## Purpose and scope

This plan states which sections and categories of the standard the installation has to be
qualified to, in which installation zone, by which method and on which article. It covers
the kit and the payload interface: the payload is qualified by its supplier, and this plan
covers what the installation does to it.

Two things are deliberately not done here. First, a category is not invented: the standard
is not part of this repository, so a category is written down only where a declared input of
the study and a public statement about the standard fix it, and every other entry names what
the category depends on. Second, no compliance is claimed: the plan says what will show it,
and the states below are what the study can reach without an article.

The category of a section encodes the installation zone, and the zone definition belongs to
the platform. The closing authority is therefore joint:

> The design organisation with the platform installer and the competent authority. The category of a section is a joint decision with the platform, because the category encodes the installation zone the platform owns.

## Why each selection is what it is

### Section 4 — Temperature and Altitude

The external bay is unpressurised external mounting, which is the D family. The declared payload environment is -40 to +55 degrees operating and -55 to +85 storage, against the -55 to +85 the section spans, so the declared envelope sits inside the section with no margin at the storage limits.

- **Z-01**: category D — the severity number (D1, D2 or D3) and the altitude profile, which follow from the platform design altitude still open.
- **Z-02**: category open on the family and the severity number for an unpressurised compartment: the published summary places A1 at a pressurised cockpit and D3 at unpressurised external mounting, and the intermediate families are not documented outside the standard.

Method: TEST on payload and kit first article, installed on the platform. State: PLANNED.

Limitation: The ground survival and operating temperatures of the kit itself are not declared: only the payload envelope is, and the kit carries no powered item except the protection assembly.

Closing action: The platform declares its design altitude and compartment map; the categories follow.

### Section 5 — Temperature Variation

The section ramps the equipment between its temperature extremes; the ramp rate belongs to the platform thermal environment and is not declared.

- **Z-01**: category open on the ramp rate of the zone.
- **Z-02**: category open on the ramp rate of the compartment.

Method: TEST on payload and kit first article. State: OPEN.

Limitation: No thermal model of the installation exists in this study.

### Section 6 — Humidity

Both zones are unpressurised and exposed to condensation; the published severities are standard and severe, and the choice follows from how wet the zone is in service.

- **Z-01**: category open on whether the standard or the severe severity applies.
- **Z-02**: category open on whether the standard or the severe severity applies.

Method: TEST on kit first article, with the interface plate and the harnesses installed. State: OPEN.

Limitation: The sealing and drainage provisions are designed but not validated against a severity level.

### Section 7.2 — Operational Shock

Operational shock applies to equipment installed on rotorcraft, and the published statement is that rotorcraft installations face the most demanding profiles.

- **Z-01**: category open on the level.
- **Z-02**: category open on the level.

Method: TEST on kit first article with a mass-representative payload. State: PLANNED.

Limitation: A representative payload mass is used in place of the real payload.

### Section 7.3 — Crash Safety

The crash safety test applies where equipment coming loose could present a hazard in an emergency landing, such as fuel system and evacuation equipment. A belly installation outside the cabin, the fuel bays and the evacuation routes is not such a place, so the section is not applied and the crash inertia loads are instead carried by the structural analysis.

- **Z-01**: the section does not apply.

Method: ANALYSIS. State: ASSESSED.

Limitation: The structural analysis is quasi-static and the crash case rests on declared platform factors rather than on a clause of 27.561 for a belly installation.

### Section 8 — Vibration

For a rotary wing installation the robust categories R and U apply, tested sine-on-random; U repeats the exposure three times where R runs once. The existing structural resonance estimate is a separate limitation and does not qualify the equipment.

- **Z-01**: category R or U — the curve, which comes from the categorisation by aircraft type and equipment location, and the choice between R and U still open.
- **Z-02**: category R or U — the curve, as above still open.

Method: TEST on kit first article with the payload, before and after the endurance exposure. State: PLANNED.

Limitation: The resonance separation is not demonstrated (VER011): the single degree of freedom estimate lands inside the rotor bands, and neither the test above nor the analysis can close that until the modes are measured.

### Section 9 — Explosive Atmosphere

The section applies to zones where fuel vapour may accumulate. The belly bay and the distribution panel are not fuel vapour zones, and the platform confirms it because the fuel system layout is outside this study.

- **Z-01**: the section does not apply.
- **Z-02**: the section does not apply.

Method: REVIEW. State: ASSESSED.

Limitation: The non-applicability rests on the platform confirming that no fuel vent or tank zone reaches the installation.

### Section 10 — Waterproofness

Category T covers externally mounted equipment subject to direct rainfall and washing, which is the belly bay. The interior bay is not exposed to water.

- **Z-01**: category T.
- **Z-02**: the section does not apply.

Method: TEST on kit first article, installed, including the connectors and the harness entries. State: PLANNED.

Limitation: The washing procedure and frequency come from the operator and are not declared.

### Section 11 — Fluids Susceptibility

The published fluid families are hydraulic fluid, fuels, lubricating oils, de-icing and anti-icing compounds, cleaning agents and extinguishing agents. The belly bay sees what drips from above and what is sprayed or washed; the interior bay sees what leaks into the compartment.

- **Z-01**: category open on which fluid families reach the installation.
- **Z-02**: category open on which fluid families reach the compartment.

Method: TEST on kit first article with a representative payload interface. State: PLANNED.

Limitation: The fluid list of the platform is not declared, so the test fluids cannot be fixed: the plan names the families and the platform has to select them.

### Section 12 — Sand and Dust

The section applies to equipment in unpressurised zones or aircraft operated in desert or high particulate environments, which is the belly bay.

- **Z-01**: category open on the severity, which follows from whether the platform operates from unimproved surfaces.
- **Z-02**: the section does not apply.

Method: TEST on kit first article, with the payload envelope closed and with it removed. State: PLANNED.

Limitation: The declared operating environment of the platform does not fix whether unimproved surfaces are used.

### Section 13 — Fungus

The declared materials of the structural parts are metals — 6082-T6 aluminium and corrosion resistant steel fasteners — and metals do not support fungal growth. The section is assessed by inspection of the material selection instead of by exposure test.

- **Z-01**: the section does not apply.
- **Z-02**: the section does not apply.

Method: INSPECTION. State: ASSESSED.

Limitation: Seals, grommets, marking materials, cable jackets and sealants are not selected yet, so the assessment covers the declared structural materials only and has to be repeated when the non-metallic items are chosen.

### Section 14 — Salt Fog

The published applicability is rotorcraft and maritime operation, and the belly bay is exposed to salt in coastal operation and storage. The corrosion protection scheme is declared as a provision of the kit.

- **Z-01**: category open on the exposure duration, which follows from the platform environmental specification.
- **Z-02**: the section does not apply.

Method: TEST on kit first article after the corrosion protection is applied. State: PLANNED.

Limitation: The exposure duration is a platform environmental requirement, not declared here.

### Section 15 — Magnetic Effect

The installation carries dc current in the power harness and ferromagnetic hardware, and the section limits the deflection of compass systems and magnetometers. The positions of those systems on the platform are not declared.

- **Z-01**: category open on the distance to the platform magnetic sensitive equipment.
- **Z-02**: category open on the distance from the interior run of the power harness to those systems.

Method: ANALYSIS. State: OPEN.

Limitation: The harness route is declared in the layout, but the platform magnetic survey is not available.

### Section 16 — Power Input

The installation is 28 Vdc equipment, declared in the payload interface data and the platform bus. Category Z is the 28 Vdc category for all other electrical systems and it is acceptable in lieu of category A or B, so it covers the platform whether the dc comes from a transformer-rectifier unit or from engine driven generators with a significant battery on the bus.

- **Z-01**: category Z.
- **Z-02**: category Z.

Method: TEST on protective assembly and payload first article. State: PLANNED.

Limitation: The platform generating system is not declared, so the choice of Z covers the cases instead of being argued from the platform data.

### Section 17 — Voltage Spike

The section applies to dc power inputs and the spike level belongs to the bus the equipment is connected to.

- **Z-01**: category open on the level.
- **Z-02**: category open on the level.

Method: TEST on protective assembly and payload first article. State: PLANNED.

Limitation: The platform bus transient data is not declared.

### Section 18 — Audio Frequency Conducted Susceptibility

The section covers audio frequency interference on the power leads, and the category follows the power input category of section 16.

- **Z-01**: category open on the category linked to the power input selection.
- **Z-02**: category open on the category linked to the power input selection.

Method: TEST on protective assembly and payload first article. State: PLANNED.

Limitation: The category is not independent, so it stays open until section 16 is confirmed by the platform.

### Section 19 — Induced Signal Susceptibility

The data harness carries the ARINC 429 control link and the video link along a route that shares the frame with the power harness, which the layout declares.

- **Z-01**: category open on the category.
- **Z-02**: category open on the category.

Method: TEST on data harness and payload first article. State: PLANNED.

Limitation: The platform wiring standard and the receiver sensitivity are not declared.

### Section 20 — Radio Frequency Susceptibility

The published categories run from B for routine commercial aviation to R and W for high intensity radiated field environments, and the level comes from the platform protection plan, which the interface data references and does not reproduce.

- **Z-01**: category open on the field level.
- **Z-02**: category open on the field level.

Method: TEST on payload and kit first article, with the harnesses installed. State: PLANNED.

Limitation: The HIRF environment is in the platform protection plan, which the study references without holding.

### Section 21 — Emission of Radio Frequency Energy

The published limits depend on the sensitivity of the aircraft receivers and on the proximity of the wiring to them. SYS016 requires the assessment against the platform radio compatibility limits.

- **Z-01**: category open on the limits.
- **Z-02**: category open on the limits.

Method: TEST on payload and kit first article, powered from a representative bus. State: OPEN.

Limitation: The payload emissions are not characterised in this study.

### Section 22 — Lightning Induced Transient Susceptibility

Lightning current in the airframe induces transients in the attached wiring, which the section reproduces by pin injection and cable bundle methods. The installation adds two harnesses that run from an external bay into the fuselage.

- **Z-01**: category open on the levels.
- **Z-02**: category open on the levels.

Method: TEST on harnesses and payload first article. State: PLANNED.

Limitation: The platform lightning environment and the induced transient levels are not declared.

### Section 23 — Lightning Direct Effects

The section applies to externally mounted equipment with external apertures, which is the payload on the belly, with the fittings on the outer skin. The interior bay has no external aperture.

- **Z-01**: category open on the attachment zone.
- **Z-02**: the section does not apply.

Method: TEST on kit first article with the payload optical aperture. State: OPEN.

Limitation: The test is destructive on the article and is planned with the platform zoning.

### Section 24 — Icing

The section covers equipment subject to operational or storage icing. The payload and the frame sit in a position where ice can accrete, and whether the airframe is approved for flight in icing conditions is a platform datum.

- **Z-01**: category open on whether operational or storage icing applies, and the level.
- **Z-02**: the section does not apply.

Method: TEST on kit first article with a representative payload envelope. State: OPEN.

Limitation: No ice accretion analysis of the installation exists.

### Section 25 — Electrostatic Discharge

The section covers discharge from personnel handling equipment and from aircraft static build up, both of which reach an installation whose connectors are mated and inspected on the platform.

- **Z-01**: category open on the level.
- **Z-02**: category open on the level.

Method: TEST on payload connector and kit first article. State: PLANNED.

Limitation: The bonding means are declared but the static path is not measured.

### Section 26 — Fire and Flammability

The section applies to all equipment and cabin equipment carries the most stringent requirements. The harness sections inside the fuselage and the protection assembly are the items it reaches.

- **Z-01**: category open on the level.
- **Z-02**: category open on the level.

Method: TEST on harness sections and protection assembly. State: PLANNED.

Limitation: The flammability ratings of the cable jackets and the protection assembly materials are not declared.

## Methods: what is analysis and what needs an article

| Method | Entries | What it means here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TEST | 20 | Runs on the first article. The study has no article, so these entries are planned, not passed. |
| ANALYSIS | 2 | Carried by an analysis committed in this repository, named in the entry. |
| INSPECTION | 1 | Carried by inspecting the declared design, which is in the model. |
| REVIEW | 1 | A review against a platform document, listed in the entry. |

The campaign order follows the published practice that the potentially destructive tests run
last: functional performance, then temperature, altitude, humidity, vibration, the electrical
and EMC sections, then waterproofness, fluids, sand and dust, salt fog, and finally the
sections that can destroy the article — lightning direct effects and any crash safety item.

## Open items

- **QI-01 — The platform radio compatibility limits are required and not declared** SYS016 asks for the payload emissions to be assessed against the platform radio compatibility limits. Those limits are not in the platform interface data, so the emission limits of section 21 cannot be fixed, and the assessment cannot start. This is an input the platform has to provide.
- **QI-02 — The category of a section belongs to the platform, not to this study** Every category encodes the installation zone, and the zone definition is the platform's. The plan therefore names what each category depends on and who closes it, and it declares a category only where a declared input of this study and a public statement about the standard fix it: the temperature family for an external bay, the waterproofness category for externally mounted equipment, the power input category for 28 Vdc equipment, the vibration family for rotary wing, and the sections that do not apply at all.
- **QI-03 — The kit has no declared environment of its own** The payload interface data declares an operating and storage temperature range and nothing else. The kit materials, the sealing provisions and the protection assembly carry no environmental requirement of their own, so the specifications of the non-metallic items have to be derived from the zones once the compartment map exists.

## What this plan does not do

- It does not claim compliance with any category: every category either rests on a declared
  input and a public statement about the standard, or is open on a named input.
- It does not reproduce the standard. The clause numbers, the curves and the levels have to
  be taken from RTCA DO-160G by whoever executes the campaign.
- It does not replace the structural, electrical and thermal analyses: the tests confirm
  their assumptions, they do not substitute for them.
